setup_name: Fibonacci 61.8 confluence long (fib + pivot + oversold oscillator)
time_of_day: London session into New York session
universe_filter: one or a few liquid FX majors
conditions: Daily oscillator reading sets directional bias
Price retraces into the 61.8% (or 38.2/50%) retracement zone of a swing drawn on multiple scales (year, weeks, days)
The fib zone coincides with prior support and a pivot point
Oscillator is low/oversold
entry_trigger: Starter position at 38.2%, main size near 61.8% when price shows it is turning; 15-min chart for entry timing
stop: Often no hard stop (guest later regretted this after a margin call); mental invalidation beyond the zone
target_or_exit: Next support/resistance level; aims for at least 1:1
management: Scales in from a small starter as price moves against him, adds heavily when it turns back
stated_edge: Confluence of several technical levels marks a likely turning point
stated_stats: First full year ~+$20-25k on $20k account, 9 of 12 months green; one ~$12k drawdown from no-stop scaling in
data_needed: FX data; for stocks the logic could be tested on ETFs with daily swing fibs
mcf_translation: On daily bars compute swing high/low over N days; flag when 5-min price enters the 50-61.8% retracement while RSI(14) < 30 and price is within x% of a prior-day low/pivot; long on first 5-min bar closing up; stop below 78.6%.

firm_or_style: prop (Kershner Trading Group), equities day trader, reversal style
setup_name: Late-panic washout reversal (high-volatility regime)
time_of_day: any; in crash regimes the panic low tends to come earlier/later than normal, often off the open
universe_filter: large liquid names in heavy selloff (down a lot on day), often short-sale-restricted after a >10% drop
conditions: Market in a crash regime (index and VIX extreme)
Stock under persistent block selling; do not buy the first or normal-sized flush
Wait for a larger 'ultimate' panic flush than would be needed in a calm market
Sign of seller exhaustion (selling stops making new lows)
entry_trigger: Buy the turn after the capitulation flush, not the early dips
stop: Tight: about 40-50 cents risk when targeting a 3-4 point move
target_or_exit: 3-4 point bounce; take profits quickly because bounces retrace fast in this regime
management: Re-enter the same name later if stopped; size up only when month-to-date P&L cushion exists
stated_edge: Forced/panic sellers overshoot; asymmetric reward when the turn is caught
stated_stats: R about 6-8:1 per winner by his numbers (0.4-0.5 risk vs 3-4 reward); no win rate
data_needed: high-volatility regime history (2020, 2008); SSR status
mcf_translation: Regime filter VIX > 40 or SPY 20-day drawdown > 15%; stock down > 2x its ATR intraday; enter long on first 5-min bar that closes above prior bar high after a new LOD made on rvol spike >= 3x; stop = LOD - small buffer; target 3R-6R or VWAP.

setup_name: Capitulation day signature (gap down, open flush, close higher)
time_of_day: open to close
universe_filter: index (SPY) during a bear move
conditions: Market gaps down sharply
Fast flush lower right after the open (panic, liquidity hole)
Recovers all the day's losses and closes higher
Ideally repeats/holds next day
entry_trigger: Guest describes it as a likely bottom signal rather than a precise trigger
stated_edge: Orderly selling is not a bottom; a violent opening washout that fully reverses shows sellers exhausted
mcf_translation: Daily/5-min: SPY gap <= -2%, first 30 min makes new low below gap open by > 1 ATR, close > prior close; test forward 1/5/20-day returns of SPY and long entries at close.

setup_name: Reopen-after-market-halt dislocation
time_of_day: reopening after a market-wide circuit-breaker halt
universe_filter: large caps whose reopen price is far out of line with the index move
conditions: Market-wide halt occurs
On reopen a stock prints much further from its pre-halt price than the index does (opening algos absent, thin liquidity)
entry_trigger: Trade toward the index-implied fair price right after reopen
stop: Not stated
target_or_exit: Convergence with index-implied move
stated_edge: Opening algos are not built for mid-day reopens, so reopen prints are dislocated
data_needed: tick data around halts; rare events
mcf_translation: Too rare for MCF; could log as an event study around halt timestamps.

firm_or_style: prop (SMB Capital), high-beta momentum off the open
setup_name: Pre-market range 'dip and rip'
time_of_day: first hour, mostly first minutes after 09:30
universe_filter: high-beta liquid names (e.g. AAPL, BABA, NVDA type) gapping on a catalyst such as an upgrade, with a tight pre-market range
conditions: Stock gaps up on news/upgrade
Pre-market range is tight (e.g. 20-30 cents on a large cap)
At the open heavy volume sweeps below the pre-market low
Price quickly reclaims the pre-market range
entry_trigger: Long on the reclaim of the pre-market range / break above the pre-market high
stop: Below the flush low under the pre-market low
target_or_exit: Momentum continuation; sells into large extended candles
management: Not detailed; trader stops trading 12:00-14:00
stated_edge: Institutional volume off the open drives high-beta names; flushing weak hands below pre-market lows fuels the reversal up
data_needed: pre-market high/low (extended-hours bars); catalyst/news flag
mcf_translation: Universe: gap > 2%, rvol(first 5 min) > 3, beta/ATR% high. Compute PM high/low from 04:00-09:29 bars. Signal: within first 15 min a 1-min/5-min bar trades below PM low, then a bar closes back above PM low; enter long on break of PM high (or on reclaim, variant). Stop = flush low; exit at 2R or trailing 5-min low or 10:30.

setup_name: VWAP wedge breakout in parabolic in-play stock (fade the crowded short)
time_of_day: morning after the opening flush
universe_filter: stock in a daily parabolic uptrend, gapping up again, huge volume
conditions: Gap up then sharp flush off the open (crowd shorts expecting gap-and-fail)
Price compresses in a wedge just under VWAP
Recent character: breakdowns fail and dips are bought
entry_trigger: Long on break of the wedge back above VWAP
stop: Below the wedge low
target_or_exit: Ride the squeeze; exited near prior highs / round number after ~30 points
management: Built the position over ~30 minutes once in at good prices
stated_edge: Trapped shorts in a stock whose daily trend is parabolic must cover
stated_stats: Best day of his career (TSLA Jan 2020, ~+30 points)
mcf_translation: Filter: stock up > 30% over 10 days, gap > 2%. After first 15 min low, detect 3+ 5-min bars with contracting range under VWAP; long on 5-min close above VWAP and wedge high; stop = wedge low; exit at HOD retest or trailing.

setup_name: Afternoon backside break below consolidation and VWAP
time_of_day: afternoon, after a midday consolidation
universe_filter: parabolic in-play stock that has had a big run
conditions: Stock consolidates for a long time mid-day near highs
Price breaks below the consolidation low
A large-volume red candle closes below VWAP (control shifts)
entry_trigger: Short on the break below consolidation/VWAP as selling 'feeds on itself'
stop: Back above VWAP / consolidation
target_or_exit: Cover into an extended, climactic down candle (cover into weakness)
management: Starts small, adds as the move accelerates
stated_edge: Late longs trapped above the range all exit together once VWAP fails
mcf_translation: After 13:00: define midday range (11:30-13:30 high/low); short when a 5-min bar with volume > 2x avg closes below range low and below VWAP; stop = VWAP + small buffer; exit when a bar's range > 2x ATR(5-min) or at close.

setup_name: Weak pullback against short-term bias (trapped counter-trend traders)
time_of_day: any
universe_filter: liquid index futures
conditions: Establish a short-term directional bias for the next two or three swings
Price pulls back against the bias
The pullback moves with weak momentum (small bars, overlap), not with strength; a strong pullback cancels the trade
entry_trigger: Enter in the bias direction at or just before the point where counter-trend traders in the pullback are proven wrong (e.g. failure to extend the pullback / break of the pullback's last swing)
stop: Beyond the pullback extreme
target_or_exit: Next swing in bias direction, fuelled by trapped traders' exits
stated_edge: Profit comes from others' forced exit order flow after you enter; enter where others will have to buy/sell after you
data_needed: futures data; for stocks/ETFs needs a definition of 'weak' pullback
mcf_translation: On SPY/QQQ 5-min: bias = price above VWAP and 20-EMA rising; pullback = 2-5 bars of lower highs with average bar range < 0.7x the impulse bars' range and declining volume; long on break of prior bar high; stop below pullback low; target = prior swing high + 1R.

setup_name: Positive-news gap: early profit-taking dip then institutional VWAP drift (observation)
time_of_day: open through close
universe_filter: stock with an unexpected positive company announcement before or at the open, gapping up ~10-20%
conditions: Stock opens/matches sharply higher on a fundamental upgrade
Short-term traders take profits, producing an early pullback
Institutions that decide to buy then accumulate steadily through the day with VWAP algos, often capping participation (~10% of volume) and slowing when price is above VWAP
entry_trigger: Not given by guest (he describes the flow); trader translation: buy the first pullback that holds above VWAP/opening range low after the gap
target_or_exit: Close (institutional buying persists into the closing auction)
stated_edge: Fund orders are worked passively over the day, creating a steady bid after the initial fast-money reaction
data_needed: earnings/news flag improves it; can proxy with gap > 5% and rvol
mcf_translation: Gap-up >= 5% with rvol >= 3 on first 15 min; wait for pullback of >= 30% of first-15-min range; long on 5-min close back above VWAP after 10:00; stop below pullback low; exit at close. Compare to unconditional gap-up drift.

firm_or_style: prop firm owner (Bright Trading), math-edge trader / ex card counter
setup_name: Short both sides of a leveraged ETF pair (volatility-decay harvest)
instrument: leveraged ETFs (2x/3x bull and bear on same index/sector)
time_of_day: any; rebalance as needed
universe_filter: liquid 2x/3x long and inverse ETF pairs on the same underlying with borrow available at acceptable cost
conditions: Realised volatility of the underlying is elevated (choppy two-way moves)
Borrow/locate fees for both legs are low enough relative to expected decay
Size both legs so the combined position is roughly delta-neutral (adjust for beta/drift)
entry_trigger: Short equal dollar amounts of the bull and bear leveraged ETF
stop: Not a price stop; reduce or close when volatility falls or borrow costs rise
target_or_exit: Perpetual position; trims when one leg grows (rebalance) or when volatility drops
management: Rebalance legs periodically; scaled from ~$30-40M down to < $5M in quiet 2019, up again in volatile 2020; closed everything once when clearing-firm fees ate the profit
stated_edge: Daily-rebalanced leveraged products lose value in volatile, mean-reverting paths (path dependence), so a short in both earns the decay
stated_stats: Example: +/-10% chop on a 3x product leaves both legs ~9% lower; one year he made ~$2.5M but paid ~$3M in financing to the clearing firm
data_needed: daily bars of leveraged ETF pairs (available), plus historical borrow/locate fees (missing)
mcf_translation: Daily backtest: short $X of e.g. TQQQ and SQQQ, rebalance to equal dollar weights weekly; P&L minus assumed borrow 3-8% annualised per leg; gate on 20-day realised vol of the underlying > its 1-year median. Report sensitivity to borrow cost.

setup_name: Backside fade of diluting small-cap runner (mean reversion short)
time_of_day: intraday; rejects the trade if price keeps pushing higher mid-day
universe_filter: low-quality small caps running on promotional PR or sector hype, with cash burn and recent/likely dilution (shelf/ATM/warrants), multi-year downtrending daily chart with prior spikes that fully faded
conditions: Stock spikes intraday far above its mean (VWAP/MA/daily level) on dubious news
Company needs cash / has dilution overhead; repeat underwriters known for toxic deals
Daily chart 'broken': prior spikes gave back most gains (bagholder supply)
Custom indicator signal (tuned RSI/MACD/MA variants) shows momentum fading
entry_trigger: Starter short on an aggressive early signal (cut at ~0.5R if it fails), full size on a confirmation signal, add more as the fade confirms
stop: Wide initial stop sized to the stock's own range (custom ATR-like measure); max loss per day enforced at broker
target_or_exit: Cover at the predetermined 'mean' (VWAP/MA/level), usually near the low end of the day; also exits if trend structure reverses (higher highs/lows, cross back above MA). Flat by close
management: Scale in as it works and tighten stop; allows several attempts as long as cumulative loss < expected reward (e.g. up to ~5R of attempts for a 6R target); A+ setups at 2x size
stated_edge: Overhead supply from dilution and bagholders overwhelms promotional demand; retail chasers are on the wrong side
stated_stats: Win rate ~26% per trade, average winner ~6R vs 1R losers; R raised roughly 1 unit per month in 2020
data_needed: dilution/shelf/S-3/ATM filings, float, borrow/locate availability and cost
mcf_translation: Universe: price < $10, intraday gain > 50% from prior close, rvol > 5, 60-day return negative. Short when a 5-min bar closes below VWAP after the HOD has been set > 30 min (or RSI(14,5-min) crosses down from > 80); stop = HOD + 0.25*day range; target = prior close + 0.25*(HOD - prior close) or VWAP-based mean; exit at 15:55. Add on lower-high confirmation. Include locate cost assumption.

setup_name: Parabolic climax short (volume/velocity exhaustion)
instrument: US stocks (low-float small caps, hype names)
time_of_day: any; often late morning after a squeeze
universe_filter: low-float runner where cumulative volume is many times the float (e.g. float 5M, 20-100M shares traded)
conditions: Price parabolic with accelerating slope, multiple halts
Extended ~1-2 ATR above VWAP and far from short-term MAs
Sudden surge in tape velocity and very large prints; large offers absorbing buying (soaking) without lifting
Climactic volume at the top
entry_trigger: Short into the climactic volume spike (top-tick attempt, advanced) - or wait for the first sharp drop and lower high (see H pattern)
stop: Above the high; cut immediately if wrong and retry later
target_or_exit: Mean reversion toward VWAP/averages; setup-specific 2-4R with high (~75%) win rate
management: Full size in one or two entries at the inflection rather than scaling; trims into targets
stated_edge: A holder that cornered the float distributes into the squeeze; once forced shorts and chasers are filled no buyers remain, creating a vacuum drop
stated_stats: Parabolic setup: about 2-3R average with ~75% win rate (his history)
data_needed: float; tape/L2 for soaking; halt data
mcf_translation: Universe: gap/intraday gain > 30%, cumulative volume > 3x float (needs float). Signal: 5-min bar with volume > 3x 20-bar avg, close > VWAP + 2*ATR(5-min, 14), upper wick > 50% of range or close < open. Short next bar below signal-bar low; stop = signal-bar high; target = VWAP or 3R; exit 15:55.

setup_name: H pattern / lower high after parabolic drop
time_of_day: after the parabolic top
universe_filter: parabolic runner that has topped
conditions: Parabolic run tops on heavy volume
Sharp first drop (vacuum)
Bounce fails to make a new high, forming a lower high / curl down
entry_trigger: Short as the bounce rolls over below the lower high
stop: Above the lower high (or above the day high, more conservative)
target_or_exit: Trail with pivots (prior bounce highs) on a trending-down backside; or VWAP/prior support
management: Trail stop to just above each new lower high
stated_edge: Defined risk against a failed retest; buyers exhausted after the climax
mcf_translation: Universe: intraday gain > 30%, rvol > 5. After HOD, require a drop >= 40% of (HOD - open) within 30 min, then a bounce retracing 38-62% that fails; short on 5-min close below the bounce's first bar low; stop = bounce high; trail stop at last 5-min swing high; exit 15:55.

setup_name: Backside bounce short
time_of_day: after backside confirmed
universe_filter: small cap already in a confirmed intraday downtrend after a run
conditions: Stock is backside (lower highs/lower lows, below VWAP)
Sharp short-covering or PR-driven pop into prior resistance
entry_trigger: Short the pop as it stalls
stop: Above the pop high
target_or_exit: Prior low / trend continuation
management: Trail with pivots
stated_edge: Bounces in a backside name are covering, not new demand
mcf_translation: After backside condition (price < VWAP, 3 lower highs on 5-min), short when a 5-min bar rallies >= 1 ATR into VWAP or prior swing high and closes in lower half; stop above bar high; target prior low.

setup_name: Market-leader dip/flag continuation and failed-short long
time_of_day: any
universe_filter: stocks with strong fundamental story and daily relative strength, making new highs (e.g. 2020 ZM, PTON, NVDA, CRM)
conditions: Daily uptrend, outperforming market
Intraday pullback to a moving average or to a prior breakout level, or a flag/pennant forms
Or: an intraday short signal (level break) fails to follow through
entry_trigger: Long on the flag break / bounce off prior breakout level / reclaim after failed breakdown
stop: Below the pullback low / failed-break low
target_or_exit: Trail under higher lows; may hold overnight only if trade is a winner
management: Trail to below previous pivot lows rather than fixed cents
stated_edge: Join the bigger trend at a cheap short-term price; failed shorts in leaders fuel squeezes
mcf_translation: Universe: close > 50-day MA, within 5% of 52-week high, 3-month RS top decile. Intraday: price pulls back to VWAP or 20-EMA (5-min) or to prior-day high; long on 5-min close back above prior bar high; stop below pullback low; trail under each 5-min higher low; optional overnight hold if up > 1R at close.

setup_name: Index reconstitution anticipation (Russell 1000/2000 boundary names)
time_of_day: positions built in the months before the rank date; exits around effective date (close)
universe_filter: stocks ranked near an index's market-cap cutoff (e.g. ranks ~800-1200 for the Russell 1000 boundary)
conditions: Estimate market-cap rank on the rank date from current prices
Names just outside the index that are likely to be added have more upside than downside (asymmetric)
Names barely inside that may be deleted have more downside than upside
Conviction rises as the announcement nears; strongest short-term momentum as certainty builds
entry_trigger: Buy likely adds / short likely deletes ahead of the announcement; size by inclusion probability (option-like)
target_or_exit: Exit into index-fund demand on or before the effective date (passive funds trade at the close)
management: Also used as a risk filter: stat-arb models should not fade names hit by index flows
stated_edge: Passive funds must buy/sell mechanically regardless of price; being early captures their impact
data_needed: historical shares outstanding / market cap ranks, index constituent history and announcement/effective dates
mcf_translation: Daily bars + market cap: each year estimate rank on the Russell rank day (late April/May); long stocks ranked 1001-1100 with rising cap trend, short ranks 900-1000 with falling cap; hold to the reconstitution close (late June). Also add an MCF filter that flags known index add/delete dates to avoid fading those flows.

firm_or_style: ex-prop, own fund (Habitus Capital), discretionary futures with systematic filters
setup_name: Filtered breakout in a volatile market (low-volume rush + one-time-framing confirmation)
instrument: futures (gold, oil, FX, indices, bonds; ~10 markets)
time_of_day: any; he suggests restricting trading to e.g. first and last hour as a self-imposed rule
universe_filter: only markets flagged in the morning by a filter sheet: elevated volatility, order flow/momentum, no strong opposing correlation or fundamental trend, neutral positioning
conditions: Market regime filter = volatile (wider ranges favour breakouts)
Price approaches a defined breakout level (e.g. weekly/double-top level)
Trade direction does not fight strong cross-market correlation or fundamental trend
Positioning neutral (not already crowded)
entry_trigger: Break of the trigger level, executed manually when the signal fires
stop: Predefined on a 'cue card' for the strategy, tight; size computed from stop distance by a risk tool
target_or_exit: Predefined target; exit early if the two expected 'objective facts' fail
management: Validity checks after entry: price should rush away leaving a low-volume area just past the break, and bars should 'one-time frame' (no prior bar low taken out in an upside break). If not, reduce/exit
stated_edge: A true breakout draws new participants and few sellers, so price moves quickly through the levels just beyond the trigger
data_needed: futures data for his markets; for stocks/ETFs volume-at-price is approximable from 1-min bars
mcf_translation: On SPY/QQQ or liquid stocks: regime filter ATR(14,daily)/price above 60-day median; level = prior-day high or N-day high; long on 5-min close above level; validity check: next 2 bars each make a higher low than the previous bar and price stays > level + 0.25*ATR(5-min); otherwise exit at bar 3 close. Stop below breakout bar low; target 2R.

firm_or_style: prop (SMB Capital / Kershner Trading Group), intraday + swing
setup_name: Low-float blow-off top: intraday short plus overnight core for multi-day retracement
time_of_day: topping day intraday; core held overnight only if the stock closes weak
universe_filter: low float that has run hard over several days (e.g. $10 to $30 or +300%), with likely dilution/offering ahead
conditions: Final day shows range (ATR) expansion versus prior days (e.g. +$7 vs prior ~$3/day)
Largest 1-min/5-min volume candle of the move followed immediately by a 'kill' candle reversal
Price breaks below the 1-day VWAP, makes a lower high, and looks to break the 2-day (multi-day) VWAP
Confirmation across several timeframes
entry_trigger: Short the lower high / break of VWAP; split into an intraday piece (target 2-day VWAP / day's open) and a core swing piece
stop: Intraday: above the lower high; overnight: stop-out level next morning sized so the loss is capped at that day's realised profit in the name
target_or_exit: Intraday piece covered at the 2-day VWAP or open; core held for 50-75% retracement of the run over 2-3 days if the stock closes weak
management: Never open a fresh overnight short just before the close; fund overnight risk with the day's profits in the same name
stated_edge: After the climax, later days retrace on lower volume; trapped buyers and dilution supply drive a multi-day fade, which day-only traders miss
stated_stats: Day 2 often retraces ~30% of the run on lower volume (his observation)
data_needed: float, dilution filings; multi-day VWAP can be computed from bars
mcf_translation: Universe: price < $20, 5-day return > 100%, today's range > 1.5x prior 5-day ATR. Signal: after HOD, 5-min bar volume rank #1 of day followed by a close below 1-day VWAP; short on lower high below HOD; intraday exit at 2-day VWAP; hold 50% to next days if close in bottom 25% of range and below VWAP; next-day stop at prior-day high; exit after 3 days or at 50% retracement of the run.

setup_name: Hot-theme sympathy laggard breakout (swing long)
instrument: US stocks incl. OTC / small caps
time_of_day: entry during the day on breakout/hold of resistance
universe_filter: basket of stocks in a theme that is heating up (crypto/blockchain, cannabis, shipping, COVID vaccines); theme detected by many names in the basket trading abnormal volume and percentage gains, chatter among traders/Twitter
conditions: One leader in the theme has already made a large move (e.g. +100-500%)
Candidate laggard has not moved yet, has a long consolidation, and breaks out of its daily range then holds above resistance
Driver of the theme (e.g. Bitcoin) keeps trending
Enough liquidity to exit; check prior runs, float, dilution history
entry_trigger: Buy while it holds above the broken resistance; add on break of the previous pivot high
stop: Below the level where the breakout is invalid (e.g. back under the range)
target_or_exit: Pre-written staged targets (e.g. trim one fifth at the first target); exit on change of character (loses VWAP/trend on hourly or multi-day VWAP)
management: Risk 50-100% of daily stop on such A+ swings (vs ~10% per intraday name); written if-then plan to avoid early profit taking
stated_edge: Once the leader moves, traders rotate into sympathy names with better reward/risk; laggards follow the leader
stated_stats: Best trade of career: entered ~$0.20 with stop $0.10, ran to ~$1.58 in ~3 weeks
data_needed: sector/theme membership lists; OTC data
mcf_translation: Define theme baskets (e.g. crypto miners, EV, cannabis). Signal: leader in basket up > 100% in 10 days and >= 3 basket names with rvol > 3. Candidate: basket member with 20-day return < 30% that closes above its 60-day high on rvol > 2. Long next day; stop below the 60-day high level; trim 20% at +100%, trail with 10-day low; time stop 20 days.

firm_or_style: prop (Seven Points Capital), intraday shorts + swing longs
setup_name: Daily tight-consolidation breakout (swing long, Kullamagi-style)
time_of_day: entry on breakout day, timed with opening range / 5-min chart
universe_filter: stocks strong over the past 2-6 months; avoid cash-burning dilutive small caps (his win rate there ~10%)
conditions: Prior strong advance
Tight consolidation for days to weeks (flag, ascending/descending triangle, flat level)
Price breaking out of the pattern; not too extended intraday at entry
entry_trigger: Buy the daily breakout (opening range break or a 5-min dip on the breakout day)
stop: Below the low of the breakout day
target_or_exit: Trim small pieces into strength; trail the core with the 10 or 20 EMA on the daily chart
management: Do not sell the core on the first pullback (lesson: sold EV breakouts that doubled within days)
stated_edge: Classic momentum breakout continuation in leading stocks in a strong market
stated_stats: Swing account win rate ~37-40% with ~5-6:1 average reward/risk
mcf_translation: Daily: 63-day return top 10% of universe, price > $10, ADR% > 3; consolidation = last 5-15 days range < 0.5x prior 20-day ATR-range and close within 10% of 20-day high. Entry: intraday break above consolidation high (5-min close above). Stop = breakout-day low. Exit: daily close below 10-EMA (variant 20-EMA); sell 1/3 at +3R.

setup_name: Intraday downtrend short with share recycling (add on red candle at lower high)
instrument: US stocks (small caps, high beta incl. TSLA)
time_of_day: any; hold time now up to ~3 hours
universe_filter: overextended small caps or high-beta names in an intraday downtrend; sector baskets of 10-15 names to judge relative weakness
conditions: Stock trending down on 5-min with lower highs, hourly chart used for big picture
Shorts/adds only on a red 5-min candle after a lower high has formed (preferably as it breaks the prior candle's low)
entry_trigger: Short on the red candle curling down from a lower high
stop: Above the lower high / per-trade risk = 1/6-1/8 of daily lockout
target_or_exit: Cover part (quarter to half) into each washout, re-short the next lower high; cover fully when price is far from its mean on a huge-volume bar
management: If a sector closes weak on all timeframes, hold ~a quarter of the position overnight for gap-down
stated_edge: Trend persistence; recycling lowers average risk and captures several legs
stated_stats: 2020 reward/risk often 8-10:1 vs 2-4:1 before
mcf_translation: Condition: price < VWAP and below 20-SMA(5-min) with 2+ lower highs. Short when a 5-min bar closes red and below prior bar low after a bar that made a lower high; stop above that lower high; cover 50% when price < 20-SMA - 2*ATR(5-min); re-add on next qualifying red bar; full exit on volume-climax rule or 15:55.

setup_name: Washout flip long (extension from mean + volume climax + uptick)
time_of_day: any
universe_filter: liquid names in a sharp intraday selloff
conditions: Price extended far below its mean (20-SMA on 5-min and/or VWAP)
A massive volume bar prints (stop-outs, max pain)
Price starts to uptick
entry_trigger: Buy on upticks after the climax bar (often still on the red candle), adding as it works
stop: Tight hard stop below the washout low
target_or_exit: Bounce back toward the mean; trim/exit if the bounce curls down again
management: Cover any short fully before flipping
stated_edge: After capitulation volume there is little selling left
mcf_translation: Signal: 5-min close < 20-SMA - 3*ATR(5-min,14) (or < VWAP - 2.5 stdev bands) and bar volume > 3x 20-bar average; long on next bar trading above the climax bar's close/high; stop = climax low - 0.1*ATR; target = 20-SMA or VWAP; time stop 6 bars.

setup_name: Momentum breakout from tight consolidation with opening-range-high entry
instrument: US stocks (liquid leaders, mostly mid/large caps)
horizon: swing (days-weeks; core held for months if trend continues)
time_of_day: entry at the open: break of 1-min, 5-min or 60-min opening range high on the breakout day
universe_filter: top ~2% of stocks by performance over 1, 3, 6, 12 and 18 months; dollar volume above a liquidity cutoff (he uses ~$150M/day now, ~$20M earlier); ideally a fundamental driver (strong EPS/revenue growth or hot theme)
conditions: Strong prior leg (e.g. stock doubled in ~3 months)
Orderly pullback/sideways range, often retracing about a third, holding or riding the 10- and 20-day MAs with higher lows and contracting volatility ('linearity')
Relative strength: held up during a market pullback
Market trend up or sideways; breakouts in falling markets mostly fail
Avoid holding into earnings/catalyst without a profit cushion
entry_trigger: On the day price breaks the daily range: buy when it takes out the opening range high (first 1-min, 5-min or 60-min candle), entire position at once
stop: Low of the entry day (hard stop); re-buy if stopped and it reclaims the high
target_or_exit: Sell ~20-25% into the first 3-5 day burst; trail the rest with 10-day MA (fast movers) or 20-day MA (slower) on a closing basis only
management: Treat any add on a new setup as a separate trade; risk and size scale with account (percent terms); use margin only when performance earns it
stated_edge: Stocks rise in stair steps; momentum persists in leaders and breakouts from tight bases start the next leg
stated_stats: Win rate ~25% (2019), ~35% (2020); profits come from ~15-20% of trades
data_needed: earnings dates to skip; fundamentals optional
mcf_translation: Daily universe: ADV$ > $20M, rank by 1/3/6-month return, keep top 2%. Setup: within 25% of 52-week high, last 10-30 days range contraction (ATR(10)/ATR(50) < 0.7), close above 10- and 20-SMA, SPY above its 50-SMA. Entry: price > max(prior N-day consolidation high, first 5-min bar high) intraday. Stop = entry-day low. Sell 25% at day 3-5 close if up > 2R; exit rest on daily close < 10-SMA (or 20-SMA). Skip if earnings within 5 days.

firm_or_style: prop (Kershner Trading Group), automated multi-strategy (80+ models)
setup_name: Trade in front of a large resting order at a round number (order-book backstop)
time_of_day: any; candidates scanned pre-market across ~3000 stocks
universe_filter: stocks showing unusually large resting bids/offers (e.g. 400k shares) at whole-dollar levels
conditions: Very large displayed order at a round number
Specific setup elements align (not detailed)
entry_trigger: Join just in front of the large order (buy just above a big bid / short just below a big offer)
stop: Exit automatically as soon as the large order starts getting eaten or conditions stop aligning (automated stop risking ~8-12 cents)
target_or_exit: 40-80 cents
management: Automated exits; he notes HFTs now play these orders and the edge has largely gone
stated_edge: The big order acts as a backstop; reward/risk ~4-8:1 when it holds
stated_stats: Risk 8-12c to make 40-80c (circa 2009-2011)
data_needed: Level 2 order book history
mcf_translation: Not testable with bars. A weak proxy is round-number support/resistance tests on 1-min bars, but the actual edge relies on displayed size.

setup_name: Crypto leadership rotation (BTC then ETH then smaller coins)
time_of_day: any
universe_filter: major and second-tier crypto assets
conditions: Bitcoin makes a large breakout move
Ether has not yet moved proportionally
entry_trigger: Buy ETH after BTC's move; later rotate into third-tier/alt coins after ETH's multi-x move
target_or_exit: Exit as the next tier begins its move / momentum fades
stated_edge: Speculative money cascades from the leader to the next tiers; pattern observed about four times
stated_stats: Example: ETH ~$300 to ~$1500-2000 after BTC move from ~$10k to ~$30k+
data_needed: crypto daily bars; for stocks use sector leader/laggard baskets
mcf_translation: Analogue for stocks/ETFs: when a sector leader (or IBIT/BTC proxy) makes a 20-day high with +30% move while the second-tier basket is up < 10%, buy the second-tier basket; exit after 20 days or when it closes below 10-SMA.

firm_or_style: retail/independent small-cap trader, co-founder of 180 Markets (placements)
setup_name: Early sector rotation laggard: accumulate quietly, sell into the liquidity event
time_of_day: accumulate in small clips across days; exit on the high-volume day
universe_filter: small caps in a sector that is starting to move (larger names in the sector moving first), company funded so it will not need a discounted raise soon, adequate liquidity to exit
conditions: A theme/sector shows early momentum, usually led by its bigger names (commodity price, legislation, overseas news)
Candidate has not moved yet
Company has cash (no imminent placement)
entry_trigger: Accumulate in small lots over days (or via a placement), avoiding showing size
stop: Discretionary: if you would not buy more, consider selling; exit when sector momentum fades
target_or_exit: Sell into a 'liquidity event' (company news, sector-wide surge, heavy volume day); target 20-50%, occasionally 100%
management: Bigger size in names he likes most; ~10% per position, 10-15 positions; in bad patches trade at ~20% of normal size
stated_edge: Sector waves bring retail volume to laggards; selling into that volume lets large positions exit
data_needed: sector/theme classification for small caps; cash/funding data
mcf_translation: Sector baskets: when basket leaders (top 3 by market cap) are up > 20% over 10 days on rvol > 2, buy basket members up < 5% with cash runway proxy; exit on first day with volume > 5x 20-day average and close up > 10%, or after 30 days.

firm_or_style: crypto hedge fund (Astronaut Capital), trend + thematic rotation
setup_name: Thematic rotation: relative strength on flat/down days, then breakout with momentum divergence, then add sector peers
instrument: crypto (top ~200 coins); analogous for stock sectors
time_of_day: any (24h market; dominant session shifts between Asia, US and Europe)
universe_filter: top ~200 assets grouped into thematic baskets (L1s, DeFi, exchanges, NFTs...)
conditions: On days when the overall market is flat or down, an asset/basket shows clear relative strength
Strength persists for ~3 days
Social sentiment and on-chain flows confirm accumulation (large holders adding, exchange balances)
Price breaks out of a consolidation range with stronger momentum than the rest of the market
entry_trigger: Buy the range breakout (Turtle/Brandt/Livermore style)
stop: Stop-loss on every position (below the range)
target_or_exit: Trend-following exit; cut exposure entirely when market structure turns bearish
management: After the leader works, rotate/add into its basket peers (e.g. LUNA then SOL); go fully flat in bearish structure and re-enter higher if wrong
stated_edge: Capital rotates between themes; technical breakouts are self-fulfilling in crypto
stated_stats: Fund up ~1,700% since early 2018 (claims outperformance vs holding BTC)
data_needed: crypto data / on-chain and sentiment data; for stocks, sector membership
mcf_translation: Stock/ETF analogue: daily, on days SPY return <= 0, compute each sector-basket member's excess return; flag names with positive excess return on >= 3 of last 5 such days; enter on close above 20-day range high with 20-day ROC rank top decile; stop below range low; trail 10-day low; then scan same-sector peers for the same breakout.

setup_name: Covered calls in neutral, high-IV regimes
instrument: crypto options (BTC on Deribit); analogous for ETFs
time_of_day: n/a
universe_filter: holdings of BTC (or liquid ETFs)
conditions: Market neutral/flat (not a momentum bull run)
Implied volatility elevated
entry_trigger: Sell a call ~10-20% OTM expiring in 1-2 weeks against holdings
target_or_exit: Let expire / roll; stop writing calls when a strong uptrend starts (caps upside)
management: Repeat weekly/fortnightly
stated_edge: Collect rich premium in range-bound high-IV conditions
stated_stats: About 2-4% per month on BTC holdings (his estimate)
data_needed: options chains / IV history
mcf_translation: Not testable without options data; could flag 'neutral, high-IV' regime from realised vol vs trend as a gate.

firm_or_style: hedge fund (Harvest Lane), M&A / takeover arbitrage
setup_name: Takeover target long with downside-anchored sizing (merger arb with optionality)
instrument: stocks (ASX takeover targets; applicable to US merger arb)
time_of_day: build within first hours/days after the stock reopens on the announcement; scale over days if it opens rich
universe_filter: stocks subject to an announced takeover/scheme; sweet spot $30M-$800M market cap where few professionals compete
conditions: Score the deal (0-100): binding vs non-binding, bidder credibility/history, funding, regulatory risk (ACCC/FIRB), major holders' support, takeover vs scheme, conditions (unconditional cash best)
Estimate worst-case price if the deal fails (start from 3-6 month pre-bid low, adjust for sector moves)
Prefer agreed deals with 'go-shop' clauses, founder-supported prices, or obvious potential counter-bidders
entry_trigger: Buy at a spread to the offer price consistent with the score (e.g. 95-97c on a $1 binding conditional bid); for unconditional on-market bids even slightly above the bid is fine because the bid is a floor
stop: Implicit: deal-break level; position size = risk budget / (entry - worst-case price); full size scored 100, half ~50, minimum quarter
target_or_exit: Usually hold to completion; trim if price exceeds the best bid by ~10% (new bids are usually only 5-10% higher), if position limits bind, or if a cheap entry has normalised
management: Hedge scrip bids by shorting the acquirer; calendar every key date (due-diligence end, scheme vote, court dates, offer close); watch for widening spreads as a warning; script/scheme deals carry more vote and walk-away risk
stated_edge: Spread pays ~8-12% annualised on routine deals plus underpriced optionality on counter-bids (cheap call options); small deals are under-researched
stated_stats: Counter-bid wins roughly ~5% of deals (2+ per year), e.g. $1.20 to $2.80, $1.35 to $3.20; fund up 7-15% in one month when three hit together; does 40-80 deals a year
data_needed: M&A announcement database (offer price, type, conditions, dates)
mcf_translation: Event study: for announced cash deals, compute spread = offer/price - 1 on day 1 close; simulate holding to completion with size = risk_budget/(price - pre-bid 3-month low); measure annualised return and deal-break losses; flag counter-bid frequency.

setup_name: Opening print fair-value fade (OPG orders vs beta-adjusted futures move)
instrument: US stocks (mainly NYSE listings) hedged with SPY
time_of_day: opening auction; exits mostly within the first minute(s)
universe_filter: liquid stocks with overnight news/after-hours moves tracked from the prior evening; any stock where an imbalance can push the open away from fair value
conditions: Estimate fair open = prior close x (1 + beta x S&P futures pre-market % change), adjusted for stock-specific news
Place opening-only (OPG) limit orders: buy well below fair value, sell short well above it
Orders fill only if the auction prints far from fair value (institutional imbalance)
entry_trigger: Fill in the opening auction at a price far from estimated fair value
stop: Not stated; risk controlled by market-neutral hedging and quick exit
target_or_exit: Reversion toward fair value; trade out in the first minute(s) or work out over the morning
management: When many fills create net exposure, short/buy SPY equal to beta-weighted net dollar exposure to stay market neutral
stated_edge: The opening print is price discovery where HFT market makers stay away; large institutional opening orders push prints too far; liquidity providers are paid to absorb them
stated_stats: Makes at least ~50% of his money in the first five minutes; places 300-400 opening orders to get ~20-30 fills
data_needed: official opening auction prints and pre-market futures; per-stock beta; 1-min bars for exit
mcf_translation: For each stock: fair_open = prev_close*(1+beta*ES_premkt_ret); dev = (open - fair_open)/ATR(14)*... ; if dev > +k (e.g. 0.5 daily ATR) short at open, if < -k buy; exit at 09:35 or at fair_open; hedge net beta-dollar exposure with SPY. Measure per-trade return net of costs; also variant holding to 10:00.

firm_or_style: retail/independent ES futures mean-reversion day trader
setup_name: ATR-gated mean reversion (fade only after 40% of daily ATR is done; spike reversion)
time_of_day: any; depends on regime
universe_filter: single product (S&P futures)
conditions: Regime classification by ATR (range expansion vs contraction); different setups active in each
Do not fade a move until at least ~40% of the 14-day ATR has been traded that day (he states 40% is reached on ~94-95% of days)
Spike rule: a 22-point ES spike within less than an hour reverts ~5 points about 70% of the time (high-volatility regimes)
His own tape-reading algo levels (internal) used for buy/sell levels
entry_trigger: Fade at predefined level once the ATR condition is met; enter full size at once (no averaging)
stop: Fixed predefined stop (example 3 points); do not exit early out of discomfort
target_or_exit: Partial reversion target (e.g. ~5 handles after a 22-handle spike)
management: Trade fewer days when ranges are tight (traded 13 of ~20 days in one month); reduce size when a setup family starts losing (regime change warning)
stated_edge: Statistical range distributions: daily range almost always reaches 40% of ATR, so early fades fight probability; large fast spikes overshoot
stated_stats: 40% of 14-day ATR reached on ~94-95% of days; 22-handle <1h spike reverts ~5 handles ~70% of the time
data_needed: ES data for exact handles; SPY 5-min bars as proxy
mcf_translation: SPY 5-min: ATR14 from daily bars. Gate: today's high-low >= 0.4*ATR14 before any fade. Spike rule: if price moves >= 0.5*ATR14 (scaled from 22 ES pts) within 12 bars, fade on first bar closing back inside; target 25% retrace of the spike; stop = spike extreme + 0.1*ATR14. Validate the 40%/94% statistic on SPY first.

setup_name: Hot-sector basket leader long using peers as leading indicators
instrument: US stocks (small caps in a hot theme)
time_of_day: morning; when one name turns green after a weak open
universe_filter: 4-5 small caps in a mania theme (e.g. 2017 blockchain names) moving together
conditions: Theme in a 'risk-on' mania phase with huge liquidity
Basket names opened weak; watch which ones turn green first
Focus on the leaders, not laggards
entry_trigger: Buy the leader (or the strongest) when peers start getting bid / turn green
stop: Not specified
target_or_exit: Hold longer than usual while the mania lasts; back off when friends/family start asking to buy (euphoria) and switch to short scalps
management: Avoid buying too many dips late in the run
stated_edge: Sector names move in sympathy; peer strength is a leading indicator
stated_stats: December 2017 alone exceeded his first five months combined
data_needed: theme membership lists
mcf_translation: Basket of theme names: at 09:45, if >= 2 of 4 peers cross from red to green on the day, buy the basket member with highest relative volume on its first 5-min break of the opening range high; stop below ORL; exit at close or trailing 5-min low.

setup_name: Opening gap run then failed break of a key swing high: fade back toward gap fill
instrument: futures / FX (works on any gapping market incl. index ETFs)
time_of_day: session open after a gap (e.g. Sunday FX open, cash open)
universe_filter: markets opening with a large gap
conditions: Large opening gap
Price extends further in the gap direction
It pushes through a key reference swing high (for an up gap) but cannot close above it (auction failure)
entry_trigger: Fade the failed breakout back toward the prior close (gap fill)
stop: Beyond the failure high
target_or_exit: Gap close / prior session close
stated_edge: Traders who chased the gap and the breakout are trapped; failure beyond a reference point shows no follow-through
stated_stats: Described as very high expectancy (no numbers)
mcf_translation: Daily/5-min: gap_up >= 1 ATR(14)*0.3 (or >= 2% for stocks). In the first 60 min price trades above prior-day high or N-day swing high but a 5-min bar closes back below it; short on that close; stop = session high + 0.1 ATR; target = prior close; time stop 15:55. Mirror for gap downs.

setup_name: Quiet coil under repeatedly-tested resistance: buy in range for a stop-run probe
time_of_day: any
universe_filter: liquid markets with a clear multi-touch resistance
conditions: Resistance tested multiple times
Price then stalls and trades quietly just below it (no selloff)
Crowd reads it as exhaustion and shorts
entry_trigger: Buy inside the range before the break, anticipating a probe above resistance to run short stops and trigger breakout buyers
stop: Below the quiet range low
target_or_exit: Take profits on the probe through resistance (expect a probe, not a 200-tick breakout)
management: Do not hold for a big breakout; exit into the stop-run
stated_edge: Markets probe beyond obvious levels to find liquidity; quiet trading under resistance means sellers are not pushing
mcf_translation: 5-min: resistance = level touched >= 3 times within 0.1 ATR in last 2 sessions; then >= 4 bars with range < 0.5x avg range and closes within 0.25 ATR below the level; buy at close of last quiet bar; stop below quiet-range low; target = level + 0.3 ATR(5-min*?) / or exit on first bar trading above level; time stop 12 bars.

setup_name: Patient reversal entry with stop-order scaling into the turn
time_of_day: any; after a long trend day leg
universe_filter: in-play stocks that have trended all day on heavy volume
conditions: Stay uninvolved until the tape clearly turns (no early small-lot attempts)
Sharp reversal where trend traders' stops start triggering
entry_trigger: Enter with stop orders as price breaks in the new direction, adding more stops as it moves in favour ('slip into it')
stop: Beyond the turn extreme
target_or_exit: Ride the stop-driven acceleration
management: Full size only at the turn; average moves in favour
stated_edge: Waiting avoids paper-cut losses from early entries and allows full size at the true inflection; stop cascades fuel the move
mcf_translation: Rule proxy: after a trend leg of >= 2 ATR(5-min) with no lower low (long trend), short only after a 5-min close below the prior swing low; add 1/3 size on each break of the next 5-min low; stop above the high.

setup_name: OTC pre-market ARCA low-offer arbitrage (historical)
time_of_day: pre-market to open
universe_filter: OTC promoted/pump names with unusual order flow
conditions: Pre-market, ARCA (the only electronic venue) offers 10-20% below prior close with no news
Market makers still bid near the prior close
entry_trigger: Lift the cheap ARCA offers pre-market
target_or_exit: Sell to market makers right at the 09:30 open near the prior close
management: Exit immediately at the open; do not wait
stated_edge: Hybrid OTC market structure inefficiency
stated_stats: Main source of his profits for nearly two years; faded afterwards
data_needed: OTC pre-market venue-level quotes
mcf_translation: Historical microstructure quirk; not testable. Lesson: venue-structure inefficiencies can be large but temporary.

setup_name: Gap momentum (index futures) and opening-range breakout (commodities) with filters
instrument: futures (ES, YM, NQ, RTY, Treasuries, FX); applicable to SPY/QQQ/IWM
time_of_day: open; range typically first 30-60 minutes; time-of-day filters applied
universe_filter: liquid index/treasury/FX futures; parameters optimised per market
conditions: Core signal: an opening gap of a given size in index futures, bet on continuation (he finds gap momentum works better than ORB on equity index futures)
Alternative core: breakout of the first 30/60-minute opening range (works better on commodities)
Additional confirmation filters, volatility filter (e.g. different settings when VIX > 40), and time-of-day restrictions
entry_trigger: Enter in the gap direction (or on ORB break) once confirmation filter passes
stop: Fixed stop (no trailing; ATR-based stops not used)
target_or_exit: Fixed take-profit or end of day
management: Same rules long and short (to avoid doubling parameters); 2-4 optimised parameters max; one contract per market spread across correlated indices for diversification
stated_edge: Intraday momentum earns most in volatile sell-offs ('escalator up, elevator down'), giving long-volatility/crisis alpha without option carry
data_needed: futures data optional; ETF 5-min bars suffice
mcf_translation: SPY/QQQ/IWM 5-min: gap = open/prev_close - 1; if |gap| > g (sweep 0.3-1.0%) enter in gap direction at 09:35 (or after first 30-min bar confirms same direction); fixed stop k*ATR, fixed target m*ATR, exit 15:55. Separate ORB(30/60) test. Walk-forward with varying IS/OOS splits; report robustness to parameter perturbation and performance in high-VIX vs low-VIX years.

setup_name: Cash-backed base accumulation ahead of an announced catalyst; sell into the news/liquidity event
time_of_day: accumulate across days; exit on the catalyst day
universe_filter: small caps trading near cash backing (enterprise value ~0) with credible new management and a stated near-term catalyst (acquisition by year-end) in a market-favoured theme (battery metals)
conditions: Multi-year base/range; price near or slightly above net cash per share
New management with a strong track record; company pivoting to a hot theme
Stated timeline for a catalyst (acquisition within ~3 months)
Supply from stale holders (iceberg sellers) gets absorbed and the tape 'runs out of sellers'
entry_trigger: Buy on reclaim of the base level after an initial failed attempt; accumulate ~80% of size through the bottom of the range, lift iceberg sellers
stop: Below cash backing (about 4.2c) to ~3.9c (52-week lows); position size limited by order-book liquidity
target_or_exit: Trim into the breakout above multi-year resistance; sell most into the catalyst-day volume ('sell the news'); keep a small core; re-enter on a later tight consolidation
management: Never add above the breakout level; size to available liquidity
stated_edge: Downside anchored by cash; catalyst plus hot theme attracts buyers; the announcement day provides exit liquidity
stated_stats: About +A$150k on the swing plus ~A$10k scalping; position up ~80% before the deal was announced
data_needed: cash per share / balance sheet, catalyst calendars, ASX data
mcf_translation: Stocks with market cap / net cash < 1.2 and 1-year range compression; enter on close back above the 60-day range midpoint; stop at net-cash price - 10%; exit 50% on first day with volume > 5x 50-day average, rest on close below 10-day MA.

setup_name: Intraday capitulation reversal back toward prior equilibrium value
instrument: stocks (liquid large caps preferred; also ETFs)
time_of_day: any; triggered by panic flushes
universe_filter: boring, highly liquid names (mega caps) rather than speculative small caps
conditions: Exponential/accelerating price change over a short window (e.g. a mega cap down ~4% in ~5 minutes)
Huge volume turnover: average cost of holders resets as weak hands are flushed
Price trades at a large discount to a reference value where it spent hours/days in equilibrium
React to the event rather than predict it
entry_trigger: Buy into peak panic once the exponential move and volume climax appear (reactive, not anticipatory); scale in
stop: Defined risk sized so a failed reversal is survivable; not specified numerically
target_or_exit: Reversion part-way back toward the prior equilibrium/reference level
management: Structure risk so that being aggressive at the extreme is safe; replay a database of past examples to calibrate
stated_edge: Forced/emotional selling overshoots value; risk is lowest at maximum panic in liquid names
stated_stats: none given; breakthrough trade was an exhaustion-gap play his mentor saw only once or twice a year
data_needed: 1-min bars with volume; multi-day VWAP/value reference
mcf_translation: Large caps (top 200 by dollar volume): trigger when 5-min return < -3 x ATR(14d)/sqrt(78) equivalent AND 5-min volume > 5x its time-of-day average AND price < prior 2-day VWAP by > 2 ATR%; enter long on first 1-min close above prior bar high; stop at flush low; target 50% retrace to prior-day VWAP or EOD exit.

setup_name: Perpetual-vs-spot basis (cash-and-carry) trade: short perp at a premium, long spot
instrument: crypto (perpetual futures vs spot, e.g. FTX perps)
time_of_day: any (24/7); hourly funding
universe_filter: liquid crypto pairs whose perp index draws on spot venues the trader can access
conditions: Perp trades at a meaningful premium to spot (e.g. ~0.3%)
Funding is paid hourly as the average premium/24, so a persistent premium pays roughly the premium per day
Avoid perps whose index components you cannot trade (index manipulation risk)
entry_trigger: Short perp and buy equal spot when the perp-spot premium exceeds a threshold; focus on the entry premium rather than the funding forecast
stop: None in the usual sense; the position is hedged, and a widening premium means sitting tight and collecting higher funding (or adding if capital allows)
target_or_exit: Exit both legs passively with limit orders as the premium collapses, realising the entry premium plus funding collected
management: Patient, slippage-minimising execution; cross the spread more aggressively during big events when premiums spike
stated_edge: Leverage demand from directional (retail) longs, plus scarce and costly credit in crypto, keeps premiums and funding high
stated_stats: Basis trade plus yield farming make up roughly 99% of the fund's P&L at the time; the core spot arbitrage engine is about 1%
data_needed: crypto perp and spot prices and funding-rate history
mcf_translation: Not applicable to MCF's US stock/ETF data; the closest analogue is an ETF premium/discount to NAV.

firm_or_style: Blue Lake Partners, equities trader (ADRs/event niches)
setup_name: Cross-listed (ADR/dual-listing) premium/discount fade versus the primary-market price
horizon: overnight (buy on the foreign line, flip on the home-market open)
time_of_day: foreign session (Europe/US evening); exit at or near the next home-market open
universe_filter: stocks where the primary listing dominates volume and the secondary line is thin
conditions: The secondary line trades at a premium/discount to the primary close, adjusted for what home-market drivers did overnight (index futures, sector peers, commodities, FX)
Typical edge is 1-2%; A+ setups are panic discounts of ~5% with unusual volume on the thin line
Unusual volume on the thin line (e.g. >1% of home volume vs a normal ~0.1%) means checking for news, raisings or takeovers before acting
Flow is mostly one-way: the home market leads and secondaries follow
entry_trigger: Buy (sell) the secondary line when its FX-adjusted price is below (above) a fair band built from the primary close and overnight leads; size up exponentially for A+ discounts
stop: Discretionary; widen the fair band when leads conflict; stand aside if news cannot be ruled out
target_or_exit: Sell on the home market as soon as possible the next session, via broker conversion or by offsetting the DMA position
management: Use DMA when it reduces existing two-sided inventory and broker conversion when it would grow it; can take 50-100% of the thin line's volume
stated_edge: Different investor bases value the same stock differently, and forced sellers dump on illiquid foreign lines
stated_stats: Example: bought ~670k shares at ~A$2.50-equivalent in Germany and sold ~A$2.75 on the ASX the next day; about one swing-for-the-fences night a month, clustered in volatile periods; early years lost on roughly 10 takeovers/raisings
data_needed: foreign-line prices and volumes plus FX; the US ADR vs home close is available for US-listed ADRs
mcf_translation: For US-listed ADRs of Asian/Australian stocks: compute the ADR close vs home close x FX adjusted by the overnight ES move x beta; when the gap is beyond 2 sigma, take the opposite side at the US close and exit at the next US open. This is a proxy only; the next-home-open exit leg is not in MCF.

setup_name: Index rebalance front-run (buy predicted adds, sell into the rebalance auction)
horizon: swing (days, later weeks to months as the trade got crowded)
time_of_day: exit in the rebalance-day closing auction
universe_filter: stocks being added to or deleted from mechanical indices (S&P/ASX, FTSE, MSCI, sector ETFs such as GDX)
conditions: Passive funds must trade a known size at the close of the rebalance day
Originally: buy 2-3 days before the effective date after the announcement
Later the edge moved earlier: predict adds from published methodology and broker notes, sometimes months ahead
entry_trigger: Buy confirmed or predicted additions (short deletions) ahead of the effective date
stop: Cut candidates that fall below index thresholds (e.g. after bad earnings)
target_or_exit: Flip into the rebalance-day closing auction, or sell into broker-note-driven client buying
management: Spread across many candidates near the threshold
stated_edge: Price-insensitive passive demand creates auction spikes (e.g. a stock gapping ~10% in the closing auction)
stated_stats: Returns similar in total but spread over months rather than days as the trade grew crowded
data_needed: historical index add/delete announcements and effective dates
mcf_translation: Given an S&P 400/600/500 change list: long adds from close of announcement day + 1 to close of effective day, short SPY beta; measure the net return after costs.

setup_name: Hypothesis: day traders exit at the close, so hold overnight and sell the next morning
time_of_day: buy at the close, sell at or after the next open
universe_filter: stocks popular with day traders (stated as an idea to test)
conditions: If most day traders flatten into the close, closes are depressed and opens elevated
entry_trigger: Buy at the close instead of selling the intraday position at the close
stop: None given (gap risk accepted)
target_or_exit: Sell the next morning
management: n/a
stated_edge: Systematic closing-time selling pressure from intraday traders
stated_stats: Speculative: perhaps ~10% more per year (an untested illustration)
